explanation: Where their armies already stood bounded what the three governments could settle at Potsdam in July 1945, and in the east the Red Army had put them there. The three governments moved Poland's frontiers west onto ground the Soviet Union held, consented to the expulsion of the German population east of the Oder-Neisse, and drew the occupation zones around lines the fighting had fixed. The conference ratified a distribution of force that it had not created. The claim is about the limits of the negotiation and says nothing about the intentions of the negotiators.
